draft.title: Social factors in specific phobia
card: Social factors are about a person's experiences with other people and their surroundings. They can add to a specific phobia, which is an intense, lasting fear of one object or situation.
Frightening event
a scary experience linked to the object or situation, such as being bitten by a dog. The fear can then spread to all dogs.
Learning from others
fear can be picked up by watching or hearing others. A child who sees a parent panic at spiders may come to fear them too.
Stigma
negative judgement from others about mental health problems. It can make a person feel shame and delay seeking help, so the phobia may last longer.
draft.remember: Social factors can add to a phobia through a scary event, fear learned from others, and stigma that delays help.

a.q: Ravi was stuck in a lift for an hour as a child. He now has an intense fear of lifts. Which social factor best fits this?
opts: A frightening event linked to the situation
Learning fear by watching other people
Stigma around seeking help
Delaying help because of shame
a.why: Ravi's fear follows a scary experience of his own in a lift. Nobody else showed him the fear, so learning from others is not the best fit. Nothing in the case mentions help or shame.
a.clue: Did Ravi's fear start from his own experience or from watching someone?

b.q: Mei has feared birds since she was small. She saw her older brother scream and run from pigeons, though she was never hurt by one. Which social factor best explains her fear?
opts: Learning fear from watching her brother
A frightening event involving a bird
Stigma around seeking help for fear
A fear that only a doctor can create
b.why: Mei was never hurt, but she watched her brother react with fear. That is learning fear from others. A frightening event needs a scary experience of her own, which the case rules out.
b.clue: Was Mei ever hurt by a bird herself?

a.best: A frightening event linked to the situation

b.best: Learning fear from watching her brother

problems.detail: The distractor 'A fear that only a doctor can create' is implausible and matches nothing on the card, so it is not a real choice. It leaves three working options and makes the question easier.

check.summary: The card, both answers and both explanations are accurate and consistent. One distractor in question b ('A fear that only a doctor can create') is implausible and should be replaced with a believable wrong option.
